extracted.intended_audience: talented early-career scientists applying for ERC Starting Grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for preparing and submitting an ERC Starting Grant proposal: eligibility, host-institution requirements, required proposal components, funding rules, and the ERC evaluation process which uses 'excellence' as the sole criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers of any nationality with 2-7 years of experience since completion of PhD (Extensions are possible under certain circumstances — see the latest ERC Work Programme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the targeted early-career window; consult the ERC Work Programme for permitted extensions and specific circumstances that alter the 2-7 years window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific track record and proposal quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assessment considers both the Principal Investigator's track record and the quality of the research proposal together (see 'excellence' as sole criterion under Evaluation Process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible research fields — bottom-up approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be made in any field of research. The ERC's grants operate on a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No scientific domain is excluded; selection is competitive across all fields on equal footing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution (location and legal status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted in a public or private research organisation (Host Institution/HI) located in one of the EU Member States or Associated Countries. Any type of legal entity, including universities, research centres and undertakings can host the PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legally the host institution must be based in an EU Member State or an associated country. The grant is awarded to the Host Institution (the applicant legal entity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution commitment and PI independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are awarded to the Host Institution with the explicit commitment that this institution offers appropriate conditions for the Principal Investigator independently to direct the research and manage its funding for the duration of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI does not necessarily need to be working at the host institution at submission time, but a mutual agreement and the host institution’s commitment on how the relationship will be established are necessary if the proposal is successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application must be submitted by PI on behalf of Host Institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an ERC grant must be submitted by a single Principal Investigator (PI) in conjunction with and on behalf of their Host Institution, called the applicant legal entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/legal responsibility lies with the Host Institution; therefore institutional sign-off/commitment is required as part of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and geographic flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grants support projects carried out by an individual researcher who can employ researchers of any nationality as team members. It is also possible to have one or more team members located in a non-European country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vacancies can be advertised on Euraxess-Jobs. Implementing Arrangements exist to host non-European talented scientists — consult ERC resources on such agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible costs and maximum funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Grants may be awarded up to €1.5 million for a period of 5 years (pro rata for projects of shorter duration). An additional €0.5 million can be made available for eligible 'start-up' costs for researchers moving from a third country to the EU/associated country and/or the purchase of major equipment and/or access to large facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ERC grant can cover up to 100% of the total eligible direct costs plus a contribution of 25% of the total eligible costs towards indirect costs. Budget planning should follow these eligibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calls, required proposal components and submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grant applications can only be submitted in response to a Call for Proposals. For an ERC grant application to be complete, it needs to include the administrative forms, the research proposal and the supplementary documents. The completed proposal should be submitted by the specified closing date via the Participant Portal submission service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls are published on the ERC site, the European Commission’s Participant Portal and in the Official Journal. Familiarise yourself with the Participant Portal and H2020 Online manual; see the online guide to using the proposal submission service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing rules and versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your proposal as early as possible. Deadlines cannot be changed under any circumstances. You can update your submitted proposal any time before the deadline by simply submitting a new version, which will overwrite the old one. You will get an ‘acknowledgement of receipt’ by e-mail for each submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan time for internal reviews and for portal familiarisation; use versioning to correct or improve submissions prior to the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre- and post-call preparation steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the call is published: find out which ERC grant and which call is suitable; identify the host institution and team members; contact the National Contact Point (NCP). Once the call is open: read the call documents carefully; contact the host institution and gather all details; start writing your proposal and allow time for others to review your draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NCPs, peers and other scientists for feedback; prepare administrative and institutional commitments well in advance of deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion — excellence as the sole criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated by selected international peer reviewers who evaluate proposals on the basis of excellence as the sole criterion. It will be applied to the evaluation of both the research project and the Principal Investigator in conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess and score proposals; those who pass the quality threshold are ranked. Excellence covers both the project's scientific merits and the PI's capacity to carry it out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality threshold, ranking and budgetary cut-off
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers assess and score proposals. Those who pass the quality threshold are ranked. Depending on the call budget available, a budgetary cut-off applies to the ranking list and only the highest ranked proposals are offered an ERC grant until the call's budget has been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting the quality threshold does not guarantee funding; final selection depends on ranking and available budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel structure and use of remote experts
rubrics_metrics.description: For each call there are 25 panels, each covering a sub-section of one of three domains (Social sciences and Humanities, Life sciences, Physical and Engineering Sciences). Each ERC panel consists of a chairman and 10-16 members (Panel Chair and Panel Members selected by the ERC Scientific Council on the basis of their scientific reputation). In addition to the Panel Members (who act as 'generalists'), the ERC evaluations rely on input from remote experts external to the panel, called referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Members act as generalists while referees provide specialised expertise. Names of Panel Chairs are published before the deadline; Panel Members' names are published after evaluation concludes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility checks and evaluation timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: After the deadline the ERC will check whether your proposal meets the call’s eligibility criteria. External experts will evaluate all the eligible proposals. About 4-5 months after the call deadline, you will receive a letter from the ERC giving you initial information on your proposal’s evaluation. You will receive further information as your proposal progresses through the evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult 'Ongoing evaluations' for detailed feedback timetables for calls; expect an eligibility check before scientific evaluation.
